- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.00 and model rises sharply, check for overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high if sentiment remains high.
- If model forecast peaks significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay (e.g., 0.5x sentiment decay factor).
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model is rising, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid false optimism.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30d moving avg), model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; use 30d moving avg as baseline and adjust by -10% if sentiment <0.50.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00), model often lags; forecast should drop 5–10% within 2–3 days of sentiment drop.
